feature: Feature 2 — Live Swap / Chart / Trade: the coin page, the origin band, and the buy flow
summary: The coin page is the only surface in Insidor where money moves, and it has exactly one job beyond executing a trade: prove that this coin exists because of a story we surfaced first, and tell you by how many minutes. Everything else on the page — chart, stats, tabs, safety — is table stakes that Axiom and Photon already render; the origin band and the earliness numeral on your holding are the only things they structurally cannot. The buy flow is specified as a 23-state machine because this is the one place where ambiguity costs users real money, and the failure states (slippage revert, expired blockhash, lost contact with no signature) are designed with the same care as the happy path.

screens.name: S1 · Coin page (/coin/[mint])
screens.job: Show one coin honestly, prove where it came from and how early you are, and be the only place a buy or sell can start.
screens.layout: Page shell `.shell` = grid `1fr 320px`, gap 16, max-width 1560, padding 0 20px — main content plus the persistent right rail (existing §6). Inside main, `.tpback` back button (32px tall, margin-bottom 16), then `.tp2` = grid `1fr 356px`, gap 16, align-items start. `.tp2-main{min-width:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:14px}` in fixed order: `.tid` identity header (84px) → `.tp-origin-lg` origin band (92px) → `.qstats` stat grid (58px, 8 cells) → `.chartcard` (468px: 40px head + 440px iframe) → `.tp-tabs`+`.tp-tabbody` (auto). `.tp2-side{width:356px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:14px; position:sticky; top:72px}` in order: `.poscard` (only when qty>0, ~168px) → `.tradebox` (~470px) → `.secbox` (~180px) → `.sibstrip` (only when story CONFIRMED coin_count ≥2, ~44px + 40px/row). All panels use the settled shared skin: `linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.02), transparent 120px), var(--bg1); border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.055); border-radius:16px`. BREAKPOINTS — ≤1240px: right rail collapses to a 44px icon strip. ≤1040px: `.tp2` goes single-column, `.tp2-side` unsticks, `.qstats` becomes `overflow-x:auto` with `.qs{flex:0 0 auto; min-width:74px}`; the trade panel leaves the flow entirely and becomes a fixed bottom bar (68px + safe-area) showing `You receive 231,402 FERRY` left and a `Buy` button right, expanding to an 88vh `.sheet`; `.poscard` collapses to a 52px band directly under the origin band.

states: LOADING — `.tid`/`.qstats`/`.tradebox` render `.sk` skeleton bars (existing `skel` keyframe); the chart card holds its 468px height so nothing reflows
LIVE — all panels populated, `live` dot pulsing, trades polling at 10s

BRAND-NEW T1 (pair exists, <5 candles) — iframe mounts, plus a 28px strip across the chart top: `First trades — 4 minutes of history`
NO ROUTE T2 — Jupiter returns no route in either direction; trade panel disabled with honest copy, primary becomes `Watch for a route`
UNVERIFIED MATCH — origin band in amber chrome, persistent banner, trade panel behind the two-tap gate
NO STORY — slim 40px `.tp-origin-none` bar; no earliness claim of any kind is rendered

STALE PIPELINE — `_pageLiveAt` older than 180s: a 26px amber strip above `.tid` reading `Live data paused — prices last updated 4m ago`, the `live` dot goes grey, and the trade panel's `.fine` reads `Quotes still live (Jupiter) — page metrics are stale`. The two data planes are separated because Jupiter can be healthy while our indexer is not
WALLET NOT CONNECTED — page fully readable and quoting; only `.poscard` is absent and the button reads `Connect wallet to buy`

MATCH UPGRADED LIVE — Supabase Realtime on coin_matches(mint=eq.$1) fires UNSURE→CONFIRMED while the page is open: the origin band animates from amber to cyan chrome, the lead numeral counts up into place, the two-tap gate drops away. No reload. Nobody else can render this
TOKEN GONE — mint has no pair, no holders, no route, age >24h: `This coin appears to be dead. Liquidity $0.` Sell path stays open for holders (never strand a holder); buy path closed

elements.interaction: **Categorical only — never render a numeric score.** '73% match' next to a Buy button makes users do their own thresholding, which defeats the abstain band. Three states, three treatments.

states: CONFIRMED, POSITIVE LEAD — cyan chrome, `+31m` cyan, full proof lines. The default good case

CONFIRMED, NEGATIVE LEAD — `−12m` in red #FF5C6E, label flips to `LATE VS CRYPTO`, sub-line reads `crypto posted first`. **Shipped, never suppressed** (D2: roughly a third of real detections are late; a record with no left tail is marketing)

CONFIRMED, LEAD PENDING — no crypto pickup yet, so t_crypto is null. Numeral is replaced by `FIRST` in cyan with sub-label `NOBODY IN CRYPTO HAS POSTED YET`. This is the best possible news and must read as such, not as missing data

CONFIRMED, UNMEASURABLE — story fell in a PumpPortal gap window, or left-censored entry (earliness_eligible=false). Numeral renders `—`, sub-label `NOT MEASURABLE`, tooltip explains. Never counted as a win

UNSURE — band chrome flips to `border:1px solid rgba(255,184,76,.35); background:rgba(255,184,76,.05)`. Kicker becomes `POSSIBLE ORIGIN · UNVERIFIED`. **The lead numeral is SUPPRESSED and replaced by a `.timing-pill.timing-mid` reading `Unverified match`** — minutes_early is a claim about *this coin's* relationship to the story; if the relationship is unsure the number is a lie. A fourth line appears: `We are not confident $KANG came from this story. Matched on ticker only.` + `Why? →`. The candidate is still SHOWN — abstain never means hide

NO STORY — band is NOT an empty state. It collapses to a 40px `.tp-origin-none` bar in --dim mono 11.5px: `No story matched — this coin is not linked to anything Insidor detected.` + `Search stories →`. This is the default for any coin reached by pasting a CA, so it must read as neutral, not broken

ADOPTED relation — cyan chrome but the kicker reads `ADOPTED BY THIS STORY` and the numeral is the story's lead with a sub-label `coin is 604 days old`. The real age is the disclosure; a pre-existing coin the story attached to is a legitimate buy with a different confidence story
MULTIPLE CONFIRMED STORIES — band shows the highest-scoring story and appends `also matched to 1 other story →`

elements.source: safety checks B1–B4
elements.interaction: A user must never have to scroll to a side panel to learn why the button is dead.

states: 1 IDLE_NO_WALLET — cyan button `Connect wallet to buy`. **The amount field stays enabled and the quote keeps running** — quotes need no wallet. Amount, slippage and priority are persisted to `insidor.pending_buy` before opening Privy and rehydrated on return
2 IDLE_NO_AMOUNT — disabled, `Enter an amount`
3 QUOTING — disabled, `.recv .v` shows a `.sk` shimmer, `.fine` = `Getting best route…`
4 QUOTED — lime, enabled, `Buy $FERRY`. `.fine` = `route via dflow · refreshes in 14s`
5 QUOTE_FAILED — disabled, `.fine` red: `No route for this token yet`. Auto-retry at 2s then 5s, then a manual `Retry` chip. Common on sub-60s mints before the pool indexes
6 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE — **not disabled**: cyan `Add 0.34 SOL`. Opens the funding sheet with the exact shortfall prefilled and a return contract
7 BELOW_MIN — disabled, `Minimum 0.001 SOL`
8 BLOCKED_SAFETY — disabled with red outline, `Trading blocked`, `.blockstrip` states which of B1–B4 fired

9 UNVERIFIED_MATCH_GATE — first tap morphs the button to amber `I understand this may be unrelated — Buy $KANG` for 4 seconds; a second tap proceeds; timeout reverts. Not a checkbox, not a modal — one deliberate extra tap, timed out so it cannot become muscle memory
10 CONFIRM — dialog open, quote frozen, countdown running
11 CONFIRM_EXPIRED — dialog stays open, primary swaps to cyan `Refresh quote`. Nothing is sent on a stale order
12 ORDERING — `Building order…`, spinner. POST /api/order → GET api.jup.ag/swap/v2/order server-side. 8s timeout → QUOTE_FAILED
13 AWAITING_SIGNATURE — `Sign in your wallet…`. Privy `useSignTransaction({transaction: Uint8Array})`. **No timeout** — a user may take a minute. Cancellable back to QUOTED with everything preserved
14 SIGN_REJECTED — `.fine` in --muted, not red: `You cancelled. Nothing was sent.` → QUOTED. Declining is a normal outcome, not an error
15 SUBMITTING — `Sending…`. POST /api/execute → POST api.jup.ag/swap/v2/execute {requestId, signedTransaction}. 15s timeout → AMBIGUOUS_TIMEOUT if a signature came back, FAILED_UNKNOWN if not
16 LANDING — `Confirming on-chain… 0:06`. If /execute returns pending, poll getSignatureStatuses at 1s up to 45s

17 FILLED — lime `Filled ✓` 1.6s → back to `Buy $FERRY`. Simultaneously: `.poscard` appears/updates with narrFlash, `.recv` clears, the Trades tab prepends the row with `.wal.you` highlighted 2s, balance refetches, a `trades` row is written

18 FAILED_SLIPPAGE (Jupiter 6001 / SlippageToleranceExceeded) — **the #1 real failure on fresh tokens.** `Price moved more than your 1% limit. Nothing was spent except the network fee (~0.00001 SOL).` Two buttons: `Retry at 3%` (pre-computed) and `Retry same`
19 FAILED_EXPIRED_BLOCKHASH — `Your transaction did not land in time. Nothing was spent.` `Retry` re-orders and auto-bumps the priority tier one level
20 FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_LAMPORTS — balance moved mid-flight. `Not enough SOL for the swap plus fees.` → `Add money`
21 FAILED_ONCHAIN — landed but reverted (err != null). **The one failure where a transaction exists** — show the Solscan link: `The swap failed on-chain. See it on Solscan.`

22 FAILED_UNKNOWN — network/5xx/timeout with NO signature. **We do not know whether it landed and must not claim either way.** `We lost contact before confirming. Check your balance before retrying.` + a `Check status` button that polls the token-account delta for 60s + a Solscan wallet link. **Never auto-retry from here** — that is how a user gets filled twice
23 AMBIGUOUS_TIMEOUT — we have a signature but no status. Poll getSignatureStatuses for 90s, rendering `Still confirming (0:47)` with the signature copyable. Resolves to FILLED or FAILED_ONCHAIN

INVARIANTS — (a) a signed transaction is sent exactly once; requestId is single-use so every retry re-orders; (b) amount/slippage/priority survive every failure and every detour; (c) no state auto-advances past a user decision except QUOTING→QUOTED and LANDING→FILLED; (d) a fill is confirmed by signature status, never inferred from a balance change

mechanism:
**A. JUPITER SWAP V2 — THE MIGRATION IS THE WORK ITEM.** Shipped code (`api/quote.js:25`, `api/swap.js:30`) uses Metis V1 `api.jup.ag/swap/v1/quote` + `/swap/v1/swap`. The verified target is `GET api.jup.ag/swap/v2/order` → `POST api.jup.ag/swap/v2/execute`. This is NOT a path-prefix change from v1 — it needs parameter/response remapping, percent→bps in routePlan, and an ALT format change. `lite-api.jup.ag` does not serve v2 (404), so there is no keyless fallback. New server routes: `POST /api/order` (holds JUPITER_API_KEY, injects `referralAccount` + `referralFee` from env — **never from the client**, that is both a revenue hole and a disclosure hole; returns `{requestId, transaction, outAmount, otherAmountThreshold, priceImpactPct, feeBps, platformFee, router, slippageBps, expiresInMs}`) and `POST /api/execute` (`{requestId, signedTransaction}` → `{status, signature, error, code, slot}`). `api/swap.js` is deleted. `api/quote.js` may survive only as a display-only estimate and should also be deleted so there is exactly one number on screen. PREREQUISITE: `initializeReferralTokenAccount({payerPubKey, referralAccountPubKey, mint})` must be run once per fee mint (wSOL and USDC), rent-funded, before any fee accrues — miss it and fees silently do not land. Add a boot-time assertion that both accounts exist.

**B. FEE MATH AND DISCLOSURE.** `total_bps = insidor_referral_bps + jupiter_platform_bps`. Insidor's referral has a documented FLOOR of 50 bps on `/order` (range 50–255) and Jupiter keeps 20% of it, so Insidor nets ~40 bps. Jupiter's own platform fee is published at 50 bps for tokens under 24h but measured live at **10 bps** across 25 fresh tokens at every size and router. **Never hardcode either.** Render `feeBps` and `platformFee.feeBps` straight from the order response every time. If the fee in the execute-time response differs from the displayed fee by more than 2 bps, abort to CONFIRM_EXPIRED and re-render — the disclosed number and the charged number must be the same number. Display: `total% · $amount` in a `.mini` row at exactly the weight of its siblings, with an ⓘ popover for the split, plus a mandatory uncollapsed row in the confirm dialog. Two exposures, neither shouted.

**C. QUOTE LIFECYCLE.** Input debounce 250ms → `/api/order`. TTL 20s. Auto-refresh every 15s while the panel is visible and `!document.hidden`. At T−5s `.fine` shows `refreshes in 5s` with a 2px cyan hairline under `.recv`. **Auto-refresh suspends the moment the confirm dialog opens** — at expiry the dialog's primary becomes `Refresh quote` rather than silently re-quoting under a finger. If a refresh moves `outAmount` more than 1.0% against the user, flash `.recv .v` amber (`flashDn`, 600ms) and hold. `requestId` is single-use: every retry re-orders from scratch.

**D. SLIPPAGE POLICY.** Default `Auto` (Jupiter RTSE) for any token under 30 minutes old; a fixed 1% on a live bonding curve reverts constantly and every revert is a trust event. Pro users get `0.5 / 1 / 3 / Auto`. On FAILED_SLIPPAGE, the retry button pre-computes one tier up (`Retry at 3%`) rather than asking the user to reason about basis points mid-panic. Priority maps to two tiers only: `Fast` = priorityLevel 'high', maxLamports 400_000; `Turbo` = 'veryHigh', maxLamports 2_000_000. The shipped `veryHigh / 1_000_000` hardcode in `api/swap.js:26` charges 0.001 SOL on every trade regardless of congestion; the displayed lamports must come from `prioritizationFeeLamports` in the response, not from the fabricated `0.0005 / 0.002 SOL` literals in the prototype.

**E. THE BUY STATE MACHINE (23 states).** Transitions:
```
IDLE_NO_AMOUNT --amount>0--> QUOTING
QUOTING --200--> QUOTED | --err--> QUOTE_FAILED --2s,5s--> QUOTING --> (manual Retry)
QUOTED --no wallet--> IDLE_NO_WALLET --privy ok--> QUOTED (amount rehydrated)
QUOTED --bal<amt--> INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE --funded--> QUOTED (amount rehydrated)
QUOTED --safety B1..B4--> BLOCKED_SAFETY   (terminal until checks change)
QUOTED --verdict=UNSURE--> UNVERIFIED_MATCH_GATE --2nd tap <4s--> CONFIRM
QUOTED --tap--> CONFIRM --20s--> CONFIRM_EXPIRED --refresh--> CONFIRM
CONFIRM --ok--> ORDERING --200--> AWAITING_SIGNATURE --8s timeout--> QUOTE_FAILED
AWAITING_SIGNATURE --signed--> SUBMITTING | --declined--> SIGN_REJECTED --> QUOTED
SUBMITTING --Success--> LANDING | --Failed+code--> FAILED_{SLIPPAGE|EXPIRED_BLOCKHASH|
                        INSUFFICIENT_LAMPORTS|ONCHAIN}
SUBMITTING --timeout, sig present--> AMBIGUOUS_TIMEOUT (poll 90s)
SUBMITTING --timeout, no sig--> FAILED_UNKNOWN   (NO auto-retry, ever)
LANDING --confirmed--> FILLED --1.6s--> QUOTED
LANDING --45s--> AMBIGUOUS_TIMEOUT
FAILED_* --retry--> QUOTING  (fresh order; slippage/priority may be bumped)
```
Invariants: a signed transaction is submitted exactly once; amount/slippage/priority survive every failure and every detour; nothing auto-advances past a user decision except QUOTING→QUOTED and LANDING→FILLED; a fill is confirmed by `getSignatureStatuses`, never inferred from a balance delta. FAILED_UNKNOWN is the only state with no retry affordance, because we cannot distinguish 'did not land' from 'landed and we lost the response', and auto-retrying is how a user gets filled twice.

**F. BRAND-NEW TOKEN TIERS.** T0 (mint seen, no pair, typically 0–60s): `.chart-pending` renders a 468px panel — cyan pulse dot, `Pool not indexed yet`, `DexScreener usually has a chart within 60 seconds of the first trade.`, and a live `mint 0:34 ago` counter. Poll `/api/token-lookup?mint=` every 5s for 3 min, then every 20s; swap in the iframe with a `pop` animation the moment a pair resolves. Stat grid renders `—` for everything price-derived and LIVE for Holders (RPC-based, needs no pair) and Age. **Critically the trade panel still quotes** — Jupiter routes the pump.fun bonding curve before any DEX pair exists, so buying with no chart is the normal early case, and `.fine` says so: `No chart yet — routed on the bonding curve.` T1 (pair exists, <5 candles): iframe mounts plus a 28px strip `First trades — 4 minutes of history`; never hide the chart. T2 (no route either direction): QUOTE_FAILED with `Watch for a route` instead of a dead disabled button. **`—` versus `$0` is a semantic distinction that must be enforced everywhere**: `$0` claims worthlessness, `—` claims ignorance. Pre-graduation mcap: DexScreener `marketCap` is often absent, fall back to `fdv`, and if both are absent render `—` with a `pre-graduation` chip.

**G. SAFETY — WHAT CORRECT LOOKS LIKE.** The defect is exact: `/v1/tokens/{mint}/report/summary` returns `{score, risks, tokenProgram, tokenType}` and carries no authority fields, so `raw.mintAuthority ?? raw.token?.mintAuthority ?? null` evaluates to `null` for every token, and `mintRevoked: mintAuthority == null ? true : false` reports `✓ Revoked` universally. Fix in three parts. (1) **Helius becomes primary**: `getAccountInfo(mint, {encoding:'jsonParsed'})` → `data.parsed.info.mintAuthority` / `.freezeAuthority` / `.supply` / `.decimals` / `.extensions[]`. One call, authoritative, Token-2022-native, and it works on a 40-second-old mint that RugCheck has not indexed — which is the entire regime this product serves. (2) **Three-valued logic**: `absent → null (unknown, renders —)`, `present and null|''|'1111…1111' → true (revoked)`, `present with a pubkey → false (active)`. Never collapse absent into safe. (3) **RugCheck moves to the full `/v1/tokens/{mint}/report`** (not `/summary`) as a secondary source for `markets[].lp.lpLockedPct`, `topHolders[]`, `risks[]`, `transferFee`. BLOCKS (4): B1 mint authority ACTIVE, B2 freeze authority ACTIVE, B3 Token-2022 transfer fee >0 or transfer hook present, B4 no sell route (reverse `/order` for ~1% of the intended out — buy route present with sell route absent is the honeypot signature, and this is the single highest-value check on the page). WARNS: top-10 concentration, creator holdings, thin liquidity, bundled launch, RugCheck danger label. SUPPRESSED for bonding-curve tokens: LP-burned, which is meaningless pre-graduation. **Because every `create_v2` mint has both authorities revoked by construction, B1/B2 collapse into one --dim non-signal line for pump.fun tokens and get no green tick** — a green tick that every token earns teaches users that green means safe, which inverts the check's meaning. Unknown never blocks; it discloses.

**H. minutes_early ON A HOLDING.** `minutes_early_when_bought = t_crypto − first_buy_at`, where `t_crypto = min(t_first_matching_mint, t_first_ct_post)` for the matched story — distinct from the story's own `lead_time_min = t_crypto − promoted_at`. Snapshot at fill and freeze (port the never-clobber pattern from `cluster-persist.js:46-58`). If `t_crypto` is null at fill (you bought before any crypto mention — the best case), store null + `minutes_early_pending=true` and render `first mover`; a nightly job backfills. If t_crypto never lands within 6h, `minutes_early_unmeasurable=true` → `—`. Negative values are stored and displayed in red (D2). A PumpPortal gap window marks affected holdings unmeasurable rather than counting inflated leads as wins.

**I. THE NORMIE ARITHMETIC.** $50 card → Coinbase/MoonPay ~2.5% + spread → ~$48.30 of SOL → Jupiter: 0.50% Insidor + ~0.10% Jupiter + ~2.4% price impact on a $2k book + ~0.0009 SOL network + ~0.002 SOL Token-2022 account rent → **~$45.50 of coin, about 9% all-in.** Computed live from the provider quote and a real `/order` call, never a static string. Where it breaks: (1) the two-flow seam loses the in-progress buy — fixed by `insidor.pending_buy` persisted to localStorage and mirrored to the URL, with a `Money ready` return band; (2) settlement latency of 30s–15min against a 20-minute-old story, disclosed BEFORE the flow starts, not after; (3) provider minimums ($10–20) exceed what a curious user wants to risk, so we quote the minimum up front and label the surplus; (4) direct-to-mint funding is unverified (U9) so we ship SOL-only; (5) `useAddFunds`/`useFiatOnramp` are both `@experimental` so they get a version pin and a raw provider-link fallback.

**J. REALTIME.** Supabase Realtime subscription on `coin_matches` filtered `mint=eq.$1`. A live UNSURE→CONFIRMED promotion upgrades the origin band chrome, animates the lead numeral into place, and drops the two-tap gate without a reload. Also subscribe to `story_clocks` for the same narrative so `t_crypto` landing while you are on the page turns `first mover` into a real number in front of you. **Privy access tokens live ~1h and Realtime caches channel auth for the connection lifetime — without a refresh loop calling `supabase.realtime.setAuth()`, every user silently drops off the live feed after an hour. This is the most likely launch-day bug in the whole design.**
dataContract:
**EXISTS TODAY** (per `docs/schema.md`, generated from a live Supabase probe): `narratives` (id, title, blurb, lifecycle, lead_time_min, first_seen_at, created_at, display_eligible, gate_reason, top_post_id, platforms, combined_views, …), `narrative_posts` (id, narrative_id, platform, handle, text, media_url, media_type, posted_at [bigint epoch **ms**], platform_post_id, views/likes/retweets/quotes/replies, …), `narrative_tickers` (id, narrative_id, ticker, name, mint_ca, mcap, liquidity, vol24h, holders, age_min, safety, smart_money, canonical, first_deployed, endorsed_by), `post_snapshots`, `post_meme_scores` (suggested_ticker, suggested_name), `post_embeddings`, `ingest_near_miss`, `worker_*`.

**DOES NOT EXIST — every item below is a gap this feature depends on:**

1. **`narratives.promoted_at`** — ⛔ THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY GAP. The entire earliness claim is measured from a column that is not in the schema. `first_seen_at` and `created_at` are not substitutes: `promoted_at` is set once at PROMOTE and never overwritten. Every number in the origin band is downstream of this.
2. **`coin_matches`** — the whole verdict layer, and the thing the ONE RULE reads. `(id, narrative_id, mint, relation 'DERIVED'|'ADOPTED', verdict 'CONFIRMED'|'UNSURE'|'REJECTED', score numeric, raw_score numeric, s_mint_in_post, s_img, s_text, s_tick, s_social numeric, strong_channels int, time_prior numeric, market_plausibility numeric, mint_time timestamptz, delta_minutes int, gate_veto text, model_version text, created_at, updated_at)`. Unique on `(narrative_id, mint)`; index on `(mint, verdict)` and `(narrative_id, verdict, score desc)`.
3. **`coin_mints`** — the prospective mint clock (PumpPortal websocket sink). `(mint pk, symbol, name, creator, minted_at timestamptz, program, uri, image_url, phash bytea, first_seen_at)`. Nothing resembling this exists. Also needs a `mint_stream_gaps (started_at, ended_at, reason)` table, because a dropped connection silently inflates every lead time in that window.
4. **`crypto_mentions`** — the ~300 crypto-Twitter accounts polled every 2 min. `(handle, platform_post_id, posted_at, narrative_id, matched_entity, first_seen_at)`. Required for `t_ct`.
5. **`story_clocks`** (table or materialised view) — `(narrative_id pk, promoted_at, t_mint, t_ct, t_crypto, lead_time_min int, earliness_eligible bool, unmeasurable bool, gap_window bool)`.
6. **`holdings`** — the flow doc's Holding object, which exists in no build. `(id, user_id, wallet, mint, narrative_id, qty numeric, cost_basis_usd numeric, cost_basis_sol numeric, avg_price_usd numeric, realised_pnl_usd numeric, first_buy_at, last_trade_at, minutes_early_when_bought int NULL, minutes_early_pending bool default true, minutes_early_unmeasurable bool default false, cost_basis_stale bool default false)`. Unique on `(user_id, mint)`.
7. **`trades`** — our own ledger, which is simultaneously the fee-revenue record, the slippage-vs-fill eval set, and the source of cost basis. `(id, user_id, wallet, mint, side, sol_amount, token_amount, usd_at_trade, price_usd, signature, request_id, fee_bps_charged, fee_lamports, slippage_bps, priority_tier, router, status 'ordered'|'signed'|'submitted'|'landed'|'failed', failure_code, quote_out_amount, actual_out_amount, narrative_id, minutes_early_at_trade, created_at, landed_at)`. `request_id` unique — the DB enforces the single-submission invariant.
8. **`token_safety`** cache — `(mint pk, mint_authority text NULL, freeze_authority text NULL, authority_source 'helius'|'rugcheck', token_program, supply numeric, decimals int, transfer_fee_bps int, has_transfer_hook bool, lp_locked_pct numeric, top10_pct numeric, creator_pct numeric, sell_route_ok bool, risks jsonb, checked_at)`. Today `/api/safety` is stateless, uncached beyond an in-process map, and wrong.
9. **`tokens`** — a mint-keyed table. Today the only token record is `narrative_tickers`, which is *story-scoped*, so the same mint attached to two stories duplicates its market data. Needs `(mint pk, ticker, name, decimals, token_program, logo_url, pair_address, first_pair_created_at, socials jsonb, updated_at)` with `narrative_tickers` reduced to a join row.
10. **`narrative_tickers.source`** — `'cashtag'|'llm'|'mint_in_post'`. Flagged in the research and still absent; without it an LLM-invented ticker is indistinguishable from a real cashtag and the $KANG class of bug recurs.
11. **`pending_intents`** — the onramp/connect return contract. localStorage suffices for v1; a cross-device return (start on desktop, pay on phone) needs a real table.

**KEY QUERY SHAPES.**
Coin page load, one round trip:
```sql
select t.mint, t.ticker, t.name, t.decimals, t.token_program, t.pair_address,
       cm.verdict, cm.relation, cm.score, cm.delta_minutes, cm.mint_time,
       cm.s_img, cm.s_text, cm.s_tick, cm.s_mint_in_post,
       n.id narrative_id, n.title, n.lifecycle,
       sc.promoted_at, sc.t_crypto, sc.lead_time_min, sc.earliness_eligible, sc.unmeasurable,
       p.platform, p.handle, p.text, p.media_url, p.posted_at, p.platform_post_id
from tokens t
left join coin_matches cm on cm.mint = t.mint and cm.verdict in ('CONFIRMED','UNSURE')
left join narratives   n  on n.id = cm.narrative_id
left join story_clocks sc on sc.narrative_id = n.id
left join narrative_posts p on p.id = n.top_post_id
where t.mint = $1
order by (cm.verdict = 'CONFIRMED') desc, cm.score desc
limit 1;
```
Sibling coins (`.sibstrip`) — **score → earliest mint → liquidity, never volume alone**:
```sql
select t.mint, t.ticker, cm.score, cm.mint_time, t.pair_address
from coin_matches cm join tokens t using (mint)
where cm.narrative_id = $1 and cm.verdict = 'CONFIRMED'
order by cm.score desc, cm.mint_time asc, t.liquidity desc;
```
Position: `select … from holdings where user_id=$1 and mint=$2 and qty>0` — but **on-chain `getTokenAccountsByOwner` is authoritative for `qty`**; the row is authoritative only for cost basis. Mismatch >0.5% sets `cost_basis_stale`.
Button rule (the ONE RULE, as a count): `select count(*) from coin_matches where narrative_id=$1 and verdict='CONFIRMED'` → 0 ⇒ Create coin, 1 ⇒ Buy $TICKER, ≥2 ⇒ See the N coins. UNSURE rows are excluded from this count by construction, which is what makes the ambiguous state unrenderable rather than merely discouraged.

openQuestions: Is 0.5% the right take, or do we move to Jupiter's `/build` path? `/build` has no documented fee floor and Jupiter takes no cut, but it is Metis-only routing and we own transaction assembly and landing. The research measured a 9.68 bps fill-quality gap favouring `/order` on fresh tokens, where dflow and okx won most quotes — so `/build` likely costs the user more than it saves us. Decide with an A/B on our own flow, not from the docs.

Jupiter's platform fee is 10 bps live on new tokens but 50 bps in the published table. If they flip it back, our disclosed total silently doubles from 0.60% to 1.00%. Do we display the live response value (correct, but the number moves under users) or a conservative 'up to 1.0%'? This is a copy decision with a trust cost either way.

Can `useAddFunds`/`useFiatOnramp` actually deliver an arbitrary SPL mint on Solana (U9)? This determines whether the two-flow normie path ever collapses to one. Test by calling `fund()` with a real memecoin mint and seeing whether a quote returns — do not design on the assumption.

B4 (no sell route) will block some legitimate buys where the reverse quote is momentarily unavailable rather than genuinely absent. What false-block rate is acceptable? This is a commercial decision about how much revenue we are willing to forgo to never let someone into a honeypot.

When a match is downgraded CONFIRMED→UNSURE while a user holds the position, do we push a notification or only update the page? A revoked earliness claim on money someone already spent is a real moment and we have no policy for it.
Does the two-tap UNVERIFIED gate persist per-mint, per-session, or per-user-forever? Per-session is the safe default but will annoy an active trader who deliberately buys unverified candidates.

Cost basis when a user trades the same mint outside Insidor: reconcile from full chain history (expensive, slow) or mark `cost_basis_stale` and show `—`? Showing a confidently wrong PnL is worse than showing none.

Is Simple/Pro a persisted per-user toggle, and does a wallet-connected trader see the slippage control on first run or have to opt in? The flow doc says Pro 'never shows a state Simple cannot see', which constrains this more than it first appears.
Does the `Take back what I put in` control need a tax-lot policy (FIFO vs average cost)? We compute against average cost today, which is simple but is not what a user's accountant will expect.
